message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to say "See you next year!" to my teacher R who's getting let go. Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. Teacher R was new this year and imposed his own teaching methods, which were different from what we were used to. He expected us to follow his way, even if it was wrong, and took points off for scratch work he didn't like. He graded harshly, took forever to grade assignments, and refused to go over tests with us. He also didn't offer help outside of class and was hostile when asked for extra help. The administration noticed, and we were told he's not coming back next year. We were all really happy about that. After the announcement, R checked out. He wrote notes on the board, barely talked, and went to Disneyland instead of attending review days for exams. Yesterday, as I was leaving his class for the last time, I called out, "See you next year!" over my shoulder. My friends told me I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. Is AITA (Ask If Truly Asshole)? Now, I need to think about whether this action was right or wrong. Let's consider the possible perspectives. From my perspective, I was just making a comment as I left the class. Since R is not coming back, saying "See you next year" might seem sarcastic or mocking because we all know he's leaving. It could be seen as a way to express our relief or even a bit of disrespect towards him. From R's perspective, he might have been feeling down or checked out, especially after the announcement. Hearing someone say "See you next year" when he's not coming back could be hurtful or irritating. It might make him feel disrespected or targeted. From the friends' perspective, they think I'm being an asshole. They might feel that it's not kind to make such a comment, especially when someone is already in a difficult situation. They might think it's better to leave things respectfully, even if the teacher wasn't great. I should also consider the context of the school and the culture there. If making sarcastic comments is common, maybe it's seen differently. But generally, making a comment that could be interpreted as mocking someone who's leaving might not be the best approach. Another angle is whether the comment was intended to be hurtful or just a casual remark. If I didn't mean any harm, maybe it's not as bad. But the impact is what matters. If it made R feel bad, then it's not a good thing to do. I should also think about how I would feel if someone made a similar comment to me when I was leaving a job. It might sting, especially if I was already feeling down about it. So, putting it all together, while I didn't mean to be mean, the comment could be seen as disrespectful or mocking, especially in the context of R's situation. My friends are probably right in thinking that it's not the best thing to say, even if I didn't intend it that way. It's better to handle such situations with kindness and respect, even if the person isn't the best teacher.
